FOREWORD This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by the Security Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Heavy Mechanical Engineering Division Council. This standard was first published a) b) for inclusion in 1994 and this revision has been undertaken for the following reasons:

of the standard fire test, and one more size of cabinet.

for incorporating

Security equipments play a vital role in the safety of cash, jewellery, important documents, etc, in various establishments such as banks, hotels, commercial organizations, offices, shops, etc. Normally such documents are stored in safes which protect these documents against theft and fire depending on the type of safes. In hotels, commercial organizations, banks etc, many documents need protection against the fire only. This protection may be required during the currency of their use or for a long period of time. Record protection cabinets are generally used to afford such security to paper media like ledger, account books, legal documents, etc, against fire. These cabinets may, in turn, be kept either in strong room/book room or may be kept in open halls. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, obsered or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS 14203 : 1999

Indian Standard FIRE RESISTING RECORD PROTECTION SPECIFICATION (First Revision )
1 SCOPE This standard lays down the requirements regarding materials, sizes and details of construction of fire resisting cabinet which afford security to paper media such as ledgers, account books, legal documents, etc, against fire. 2 REFERENCES The Indian Standards listed in Annex A contain provisions which through reference in this text, constitute provision of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All the standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated in Annex A. 3 NOMINAL SIZES c) IS 410 d) IS 713 e) IS 7608 6 DIMENSIONS AND TOLERANCES

4 TYPES Record protection follows: cabinets.shall be of two types as 7 DESIGNATION The cabinet shall generally be designated by type, nominal size and number of this Indian Standard.
Example:

Type FR60 - Cabinets having a fire resisting capacity of 60 minutes. Type FR120 - Cabinets having a fire resisting capacity of 120 minutes. 5 MATERIALS

A record protection cabinet of Type FR60 and nominal size 1 600 shall be designated as: Record Protection Cabinet FR60 x 1 600 IS 14203 8 FABRICATION 8.1 Outer Shell Outer shell shall be made from steel sheet not more than 2 mm thick. 8.2 Inner Shell Inner shell shall be made from steel sheet not more than 1.6 mm thick. 8.3 Shelf Shelf shall be made from steel sheet of thickness not less than 1.25 mm and not more than 2 mm and shall be of adjustable type.

Different components of the record protection cabinets shall be manufactured from material as specified below: 1) Steel components a) IS 513 b) IS 1079 c) IS 1570 (Part 5) d) IS 1732 e) IS 2062 f) IS 5986 g) IS 9550 2) Brass/Bronze components a) IS 292 b) IS 306

IS 14203 : 1999 8.4 Door The door shall be fabricated from steel sheet not more than 2.5 mm thick without any burrs and dents. 8.5 Locking Mechanism and final coat paint conforming applied. to IS 2074 shall be

The locking mechanism shall be of four way type. The dia of shooting bolts shall not be more than 20 mm. There shall be minimum three shooting bolts (two shooting bolts for size 1 000) on each side and one shooting bolt on top and bottom. The shooting bolts shall slide smoothly in recess and engage in the body to a minimum depth of 12 mm. 8.6 Locks The cabinet shall be supplied with not less than six lever dual control key lock with duplicate keys of stainless steel. Alternatively three wheel combination lock in place of key lock or both may be provided, if required by the purchaser. 8.7 Handles. Handle shall be made from cast brass or zinc base alloy or mild steel and shall be nickel chrome plated or powder coated. 9 ASSEMBLY 9.1 The components shall be assembled by bolting, welding or riveting or combination of the three. 9.2 The method of gas, arc and spot welding shall conform to IS 1323, IS 816 and IS 819 respectively. 10 CONSTRUCTION 10.1 The design of the cabinet shall be double wall type for door as well as body with homogeneous barrier material filled in. 10.2 The insulating material should not produce toxic gases when the cabinet is exposed to fire situation. 11 INTERNAL FIXTURES

12.3 Finish shall be smooth, uniformly applied and free from visible defects. It shall be smooth and shall not readily chip or flake. The dry film thickness shall not be less than 0. lmm and shall be polished to bring out lustre or be in matt finish or stipple finish. 13 TESTS AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY

13.1 Two samples known to be fully representative of the lot of fire resisting record protection cabinets of similar design and construction shall be selected on the basis of random sampling by inspection agency. Out of the selected samples, one sample shall be subjected to fire endurance test (see B-3.1) and other sample shall be subjected to fire and impact test (see B-3.2). 13.2 The fire resisting record protection cabinets shall be considered to be conforming to the requirements of this standard if they successfully complete the fire endurance test (see B-3.1) and tire and impact test (see B-3.2). 13.2.1 The fire resisting record protection cabinets shall be considered to have successful!y completed the fire endurance tests (see B-3.1) and fire and impact test (see B-3.2) if the contents (see B-1.1, B-3.1.1 and B-3.2.1) kept in the cabinets during the tests are usable. The contents are considered to be usable after tests if they are able to withstand ordinary handling without crumbling or falling apart and the writings on them are legible and reproducible. 14 MARKING 14.1 A metal plate showing Type of cabinet together with the manufacturer's name and the year of manufacture shall be fixed on the inner face of the door. 14.2 Marking on Keys The keys shall be marked with an identification number which shall not be the same as the serial number of the cabinet. 14.3 BIS Certification Marking cabinets may also be

11.1 The cabinet shall be provided with minimum four shelves for nominal size 1 600, three shelves for nominal size 1 300 and two shelves for cabinets of nominal size 1 000 and shall be of adjustable type. 11.2 A cabinet may also be provided with drawer unit fitted with minimum five lever single control lock, if required by the customer. 12 PAINTING 12.1 All surfaces, shall be thoroughly degreased and cleaned of rust before application of proof primer. 12.2 Putty conforming to IS 419 shall be applied to all surfaces requiring filling. Contents of the fire resisting record protection cabinets subjected to these tests shall include currency-notegrade paper, file, letter, record-form paper (printed, typed or handwritten). El.2 Thermocouple

Thermocouples enclosed in protection tube of suitable material and dimensions, shall have time constant of the protected thermocouple assembly within the range from 5 min to 7.2 min. B-1.2.1 A typical thermocouple assembly conforming to B-l.2 may be fabricated by fusion welding the twisted ends of chromel-alumel wire not smaller than 0.52 mm2 and not larger than 0.82 mm2 in cross section and mounting the leads in porcelain insulators so that the thermocouple head is 12 mm from the sealed end of a standard weight, normal 12 mm diameter iron, steel or inconel pipe. B-l.3 Furnace furnace fuel and air supplies shall be that the fire is uniformly distributed over faces of the cabinet and regulated to in accordance with the Standard Time Curve.

B-1.3.1 The adjusted such the exposed temperatures Temperature

bottom. A pipe of the same external diameter shall be welded to outer and inner body sheets of the cabinet. This hole shall be used for insertion of thermocouple wires inside the cabinet. After insertion of the thermocouple wires through the hole it shall be sealed by proper insulating compound from both ends of the hole. B-2.1.2 All thermocouples shall be located 50 mm from the top of the cabinet interior. Four thermocouples shall be located 25 mm from the side walls, two of these being 25 mm from back and the other two 25 mm from the inner face of the doors. For double door cabinets a fifth thermocouple shall be located 25 mm from the inner face of the doors opposite the centre door joint. B-2.2 For Fire and Impact Tests This test shall be conducted without any thermocouple inside the sample. B-2.3 Furnace Temperature The furnace thermocouples thermocouples exposed faces `face. B-2.4 temperature shall be recorded by symmetrically distributed. At least four shall be used, placed 50 mm from the of the test sample including the door

B-1.3.3 The accuracy of the furnace control shall be such that the area under the time temperature curve, obtained by averaging all the furnace th&mocouple readings, shall be within 10 percent of the corresponding atea under the Standard Time Temperature Curve for two hours. B-2 PREPARATIONS FOR TESTS Tests

B-2.1 For Fire Endurance

Conditioning

B-2.1.1 The sample to be subjected to fire endurance test shall have a 16 mm diameter through hole at the 4

The inside temperature. of the samples at the start of the tests shall be in accordance with IS 196. If the

IS 14203 : 1995 conditions inside the samples are not within the range then the sample shall be conditioned for at least 12 h prior to the tests the inside conditions. B-3 TESTS B-3.2 Fire and Impact Test B-3.1 Fire Endurance Test B-3.1.1 The sample of fire resisting record protection cabinet prepared in manner specified in B-2.1.1 and B-2.1.2 is placed in the furnace. The storage area shall then be evenly filled with contents (see B-1.1) occupying volume equal to 25 to 50 percent of the volume of cabinet. The cabinet is then locked. B-3.1.2 The furnace shall then be put on and the temperatures shall be read at intervals not exceeding 5 min during the test. Average of all the thermocouples outside the sample shall be recorded and shall be taken as the required value. B-3.1.3 The pressure in the furnace chamber during the test shall be maintained as close as possible to atmospherii pressure. B-3.1.4 The furnace fire shall be continued for 60 min for cabinets of 60 min rating and 120 min for cabinets of 120 min rating. During the tire endurance test, it is essential that at no time the internal temperature of the cabinet, as shown by the thermocouples placed inside the cabinet, shall exceed 177�C irrespective of ambient temperature. B-3.1.5 After the specified period the furnace is switched off. The cabinet is continued to be kept in the furnace and temperature of the interior of the sample cabinet is to be continuously recorded until a definite drop is noted. B-3.2.1 The sample to be subjected to this test shall have contents as specified in B-3.1.1 and shall be subjected to test without any thermocouple inside the cabinet. B-3.2.2 The cabinet shall be subjected to fire exposure in a manner similar to the tire test for the period of 30 min for cabinets rating and 45 min for cabinets of 120 min a standard endurance of 60 min rating. B-3.1.6 After the cabinet inside the furnace has cooled to about 47�C temperature, its door/drawer shall be opened. The contents shall be examined to determine their usability.

B-3.2.3 After the fire exposure time, the furnace shall be switched off. The cabinet shall then be hoisted so that its bottom is 4 m above a layer of brick rubble (30 cm depth) on a heavy concrete base, and then dropped. Twenty minutes shall be elapsed from the time the furnace fire is extinguished until the cabinet is dropped. B-3.2.4 After the impact, the cabinet examined, for deformation/damage. shall be

B-3.2.5 Immediately after the impact, the cabinet shall be inverted, put back in the test furnace, and again subjected to a standard tire exposure for the period of 30 min for cabinets of 60 min rating and 45 min for cabinets of 120 min rating. Then the sample shall be allowed to cool to less than 47�C without opening the furnace. B-3.2.6 After cabinet has cooled to less than 47�C the door/drawer shall be opened to examine its heat insulating properties, as evident by the usability of the contents.
